title: Streamline init-pass and async mem-merge to cut host CPU-GPU latency
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: The runtime's init-pass (what we commonly call prefill) currently performs many small host->device memcpy operations and synchronous control-plane handoffs. On busy workloads this creates CPU-side threadpool contention, frequent context switches, and duplicated memcpy fanout across shards. Goal: Reduce host overhead for the init-pass by introducing an async mem-merge stage and a lightweight control-plane batching mechanism that groups small priming writes, minimizes thread wakeups, and surfaces explicit kernel hints for the scheduler. This ticket covers design, spike implementation, integration tests, and performance validation on dedicated and hosted stacks.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p50 init-pass latency reduction >= 25% on benchmark traces with short sequences (<=64 tokens)
Host CPU utilization during steady-state init-pass reduced by >= 30% on 32-concurrency test
No regression in decode-path latency (p99 <= baseline + 5ms)
Fallback path that preserves correctness when async mem-merge is disabled via runtime flag
Automated microbench harness and CI job that measures memcpy throughput and thread wakeup counts added
tasks: Spike: implement in-process async mem-merge buffer and measure memcpy aggregation (Liam)
Design: define control-plane batching protocol and kernel hint metadata (Aisha)
Implement: integrate mem-merge into init-pass path with opt-in runtime flag (Liam)
Tests: unit tests for merged memcpy correctness + fuzz for interleaved requests (QA)
Performance: run nightly microbench on dedicated cluster and collect traces (SRE)
Docs: update runtime config docs and add guidance for tuning mem-merge and batch windows (Devexp)
comments: 2025-01-17 - Aisha: Spike showed promise. Aggregating small memcpy into 8KB-aligned batches reduced kernel launches. Observed fewer thread wakeups in Linux perf samples.

2025-01-22 - Liam: Implemented prototype using per-worker ring buffer + single async submit. Initial microbench: 28% lower p50 for 32-concurrency, but p99 increased by ~3ms under synthetic jitter. Investigating whether scheduler backpressure causes tail impact.
2025-01-30 - Design review: PM and Kernel team raised concern about GPU memory pressure when coalescing many requests; proposal added adaptive windowing based on live free memory metric.

2025-02-05 - Liam: Added kernel-selection hint metadata to requests so the device-side kernel picker can prefer low-overhead memcpy kernels for merged writes. Early results show reduced kernel diversity and slightly better cache-locality.

2025-02-10 - QA: Added fuzz scenario for request interleaving; found edge case where partial merge + preemption could reorder KV cache priming. Patched to include sequence IDs and integrity check before submit.
2025-02-12 - Aisha: Creating performance CI job and wiring dashboard. Next step: run full regression on dedicated-20 and prepare RFC for rollout plan (canary config + runtime flag control).
